10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates simulating local training on separate devices and aggregating only their weight updates, already covered in this topic.

code.content:
def local_device_training(local_data, shared_weight, learning_rate=0.1):
    # already covered as local training on each device in this topic
    gradient = sum((shared_weight * x - y) * x for x, y in local_data) / len(local_data)
    local_update = -learning_rate * gradient
    return local_update  # genuinely only the update is returned, never local_data itself

# already covered as local, private data staying on each device in this topic
device_a_data = [(1.0, 0.9), (2.0, 1.8), (3.0, 2.7)]
device_b_data = [(1.0, 1.1), (2.0, 2.3), (3.0, 3.4)]
device_c_data = [(1.0, 0.8), (2.0, 1.7), (3.0, 2.5)]

shared_weight = 0.6

# already covered as aggregating updates not data in this topic
updates = []
for device_id, local_data in enumerate([device_a_data, device_b_data, device_c_data]):
    update = local_device_training(local_data, shared_weight)
    updates.append(update)
    print(f"Device {device_id} (already covered in this topic) sends only its own weight update: {update:.4f}")

averaged_update = sum(updates) / len(updates)
new_shared_weight = shared_weight + averaged_update
print(f"\nAveraged update applied to the shared model (already covered in this topic): {averaged_update:.4f}")
print(f"New shared weight: {new_shared_weight:.4f}")
print("\nNotice: none of the raw device_a_data, device_b_data, or device_c_data ever left its own device")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Federated learning trains one shared model across many devices, each keeping its own data local.
Unlike distributed training, the raw data never leaves each individual participating device at all.
Privacy rules or practical constraints sometimes prevent centralizing raw data in one place.
Each device trains the shared model locally, producing a local weight update, not raw data.
Only local weight updates get sent to a central server, reusing gradient synchronization ideas.
Because raw data never leaves the device, federated learning offers real privacy benefits.
Different devices often have very different data distributions, making combining updates trickier.
Federated learning suits privacy-sensitive, distributed data; ordinary distributed training suits centralizable data.
